findings.evidence: a child was born... February 16, 1838... between the twin poles of Beacon Hill and the rocky fields of Quincy

Winter and summer, cold and heat, town and country, force and freedom... Town was restraint, law, unity. Country... was liberty, diversity, outlawry... From earliest childhood the boy was accustomed to feel that, for him, life was double.
He hung about the library; handled books... the smell of peaches... shaped by rituals and arguments of Boston politics and pulpit; he recoils from schools
1848, Free Soil maneuvers, Sumner's rise... This was the boy's first lesson in practical politics... education in America is as much a matter of party, press, and social friction as of books

Harvard College... taught little, and that little ill... His first lecture was his last. He needed no more than one hour to see that he had made another failure in education... The Civil Law existed as lecture in its deadliest thirteenth-century form.

Italian sunlight... Captain Palmer took him with the officers to make an evening call on Garibaldi... London's gray respectability... the modern mind must take its measure from force as much as from form
Henry Adams was his father's private secretary... Minister Adams sailed for England, May 1, 1861... diplomacy becomes his university
the Trent Affair... Earl Russell's polite evasions and the Lairds' ironclad rams put England's scruples on the scales against America's survival
Palmerston's drawing rooms... the paradoxes and violences of Gladstone's eloquence... the dry, implacable habits of the British cabinet

The Alabama escapes; the rams nearly do; but patience, documentation, and quiet pressure... eventually detain them... Russell's reply... announcing that instructions have been issued which will prevent the departure of the two ironclad vessels
Through these years he loses illusions about men... society is a mechanism, and the mind must find a scale on which to weigh it
In February, 1868, he was back in Rome... wondering whether his education... has taught him to read the drift of a nation that has changed continents under his feet
The postwar Republic makes him a writer and sometimes a professor, but in both roles he calls himself a failure... Harvard's lecture rooms turn quick minds into catalogues
Clarence King, John Hay, and Henry Adams had led modest existences... sits inside the operating theater of Gilded Age politics and press, but rarely mistakes access for mastery
History seems to him a contest of forces... he studies the Chicago and Paris Expositions as if they were dynamos with the covers off

the dynamo became a symbol of infinity... the Virgin of Chartres, who drew an age into a self-coherent unity of feeling, with the whirring dynamo that condenses new infinities of power without a moral map
he turns from cathedrals' glass to steel's glow and from Thomas Aquinas's synthesis to Karl Pearson's skepticism, finding that order has dissolved into multiplicity
the movement from unity into multiplicity, between 1200 and 1900... education—his and ours—must learn to think in contradictions
These contradictions gather as friends die and power modernizes its cruelty... King dropped... Hay's strength failed
The Spanish War and McKinley's assassination pass swiftly from spectacle to structure; meanwhile Hay's 'open door' diplomacy... hint at a modern pax
Russia's inertia, the Boer War's ironies, and the Boxer crisis... bombs educate more swiftly than sermons, and the Senate calls force by another name
if man is a force among forces, his mind is a function of acceleration; modern life doubles its power like coal tons

a dynamic theory of history: as new energies—steam, electricity, radium—enter the system, the mind is reoriented, the old unities crack, and education, if honest, must prepare for shock rather than repose
Chartres and the Virgin still model a unity of appeal, but the dynamo and its derivatives command habit; the modern student must triangulate from both
Adams, an elderly 'pedometer' of forces, confesses that his dynamic law may be no more than an instrument, and that the next generation will test it by living through the next doubling of speed
He proposes no program: the Senate cannot legislate unity... no press arouse ethics in an engine
More than once Adams sat at sunset on the steps of Santa Maria di Ara Coeli, wondering... history is a sequence of accelerations whose unity may exist only in our need to find one
The first summons that met Adams... was to Clarence King's funeral... Hay was dead... With them goes the last of a certain American candor

between the Virgin and the Dynamo lies the path of the modern mind, and the only preparation worth having is the agility to move between them as the forces that summon us grow stronger and less humane
